_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §AE] Regional pyramid / monument styles for ruin_builder.gd. Ruins.pyramid_style() should pick a style whose spawn.realm contains the cell's realm (data/biomes realm field, §AA) AND whose spawn.biomes contains the biome key; no match → no pyramid. Biome keys are BiomeTemplates enum names (all exist).
_help.fields: base_m: side length range. tiers: receding steps (1 = smooth). face_deg: face angle. profile: smooth | step | talud_tablero | rounded_adobe | earth. stairs: number of grand stairs (0 = none). top: none | chapel_at_foot | temple_comb | twin_shrine | hall | shrine | post_circle. interior: none | corridor_chamber | top_room. material: palette key. cluster: single | single+satellite | field | plaza | avenue | terraces (cluster_n = how many). chance: share of that biome's ruins that are this style (replaces PYRAMID_CHANCE).
_help.climb: Stair risers are ledges (§0). smooth casing = cling only at broken patches. terraces are a staircase for the valley and hold soil (spawn gate for camp-follower ground plants).
_help.styles_kinds: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DO, §DR, §DS] Entries with kind 'own' are new Ruins.Kind values (each 'name_in_play' is its KIND_NAMES entry); entries with kind 'castle' or 'tower' are styles of those kinds, picked like the pyramid styles by spawn.realm and spawn.biomes. spawn.nest names landforms.json nests; needs and never are plain words for the builder. per_world_max caps a kind. delve: direction (up, down, in, inward), rooms, heart, way_out (§CJ.4), fire_holder (delves.json). Real references live only in source (§BO). The terrace_platform style gains the fitted polygonal stone wall as its §BQ signature (§DS).

lighthouse.source: Pre-glass coastal light towers (Pharos of Alexandria, the Tower of Hercules, medieval Mediterranean fire towers)
lighthouse._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DN] Design 3 Oct §DN (Mike): a lighthouse on the coast. The lamp room is the ruin's hearth, a steady coal-fire brazier (no sweeping beam), one warm point on the headland seen from the far end of the coast road; dark means the stairwell is a den to clear before you can carry fire up and relight it. The §DM straight approach runs along the cliff top.

crag_fortress.source: Hilltop fortress-monasteries of the Tibetan plateau and the Himalaya (Gyantse Dzong, the dzongs of Bhutan, Leh Palace); notes only, never named in play (§BO)
crag_fortress._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DO] Mike, 3 Oct: its own kind, in Tibet-like country, the red band kept, no prayer flags. Battered limewashed walls in tiers up a crag, flat roofs, the matte red band under every roofline (a material, never a light: R7), one matte gilt finial on the top chapel (first guess, kept), the long stair, buildings at the foot where a camp lives if one does (§CK). The delve climbs: stores and a cistern in the rock, the heart is the chapel at the top, out by the outside stair (§CJ.4). Smoke: roof vents (smoke.json). No cloth anywhere.

temple_city.source: The temple cities of the Khmer in monsoon forest (Angkor, Ta Prohm, Preah Khan); notes only, never named in play (§BO)

root_trees.species: the place's own (§CA, §CS): Ficus benghalensis, Ficus religiosa; Tetrameles nudiflora once filled

camp.note: a living camp at the monument wears ochre (§CL's colour); first guess, Mike's call

temple_city._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DR] Mike, 3 Oct, from eight frames of the temple the forest took back. Concentric galleries of square columns, carved gopuras, courtyards of tumbled blocks, tiered towers, a moat; root-trees standing on the gallery roofs with their roots poured over the doorways (the mechanism of §CL and §DJ, here the signature). §BB in stone: galleries corridors, gopuras thresholds, courtyards rooms, doorways voids. Shade olive (R3). The delve walks inward to the central tower and out by a collapsed gallery. Size is a first guess; the real ones are a kilometre.

gate.face_towers: a great serene face on each of the gate tower's four sides, looking out over the four roads; faces of nobody by name (§BO)
gate.causeway: rows of crouching guardians holding a serpent's body as a balustrade over the moat, half scowling and half serene
gate.corners: a three-headed elephant pulling lotus trunks from the wall
gate.far_tell: a pale face in the trees at the end of the avenue (R10)

long_wall.source: Frontier walls over the ridges (the Great Wall's Ming and earlier stretches, Hadrian's Wall for the smaller form); notes only (§BO)

delve.way_out: a postern on the far side

long_wall._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS.1] A wall running over the ridges for miles with towers at intervals, broken in places, a road along its top (§DM: the wall is a road kind). The first linear monument besides the aqueduct. The gate towers' vaults are the delve; the towers vent through wall flues (smoke.json).

carved_cliffs.source: Rock-cut facades of desert canyons (Petra, the Lycian and Ajanta cut tombs); notes only (§BO)

delve.way_out: a shaft to the canyon rim

carved_cliffs.smoke: out the facade doors; soot above them
carved_cliffs._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS.2] Facades cut into a sandstone canyon wall, reached through a slot canyon (§CK's nests); the rock-cut tombs behind them are the delve. Sandstone only.

stone_heads.source: The moai of Rapa Nui on their ahu, and the quarry at Rano Raraku; notes only (§BO)
stone_heads.waits_for: a tenth realm, oceania, in RealmMap (code: Claude Code's); until then this entry places nothing

delve.heart: an unfinished head still in the rock

stone_heads._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS.3] A row of great stone heads on their platforms along a treeless coast, facing inland; the quarry's cave is the delve. The restraint rule (§BL) as a landscape: heads, grass, no trees, and nothing says why (§BQ). Waits for the oceania realm.

terraced_pueblo.source: The stepped adobe towns of the American Southwest (Taos, the Chaco great houses) and the alcove dwellings (Mesa Verde) for the cliff variant; notes only (§BO)

delve.rooms: the kiva, a round sunken room, and stores

terraced_pueblo._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS.4] Mike's 'pueblo pyramids', read as the stepped adobe towns of many storeys. Adobe melts, so an old one is a mound with walls standing in it; the kiva is the delve; smoke out roof hatches. With it, the cliff dwelling as a camp's remains at the mesa alcove nest.

stone_circle.source: The henges and stone circles of Atlantic Europe (Stonehenge, Avebury, Callanish); notes only (§BO)

delve.note: the one allowed exception to §CJ's every ruin has a delve (first guess)

stone_circle._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS.5] A ring of standing stones on open grassland or moor; standing stones are already waymarks (§BC), this is the great one. The delve is a souterrain, or none.

tower_house.source: The tower houses of Scotland and Ireland (14th–17th c.); notes only (§BO)
tower_house._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS] A style of the castle kind: a tall narrow keep inside a low wall, on the cold wet coasts and moors; lichen and moss (§DI); the castle's chimney stack (§CV).

broch.source: The Iron Age brochs of Scotland (Mousa, Dun Carloway): drystone round towers, double-walled, with souterrains nearby; notes only (§BO)

delve.rooms: the gallery between the walls, then a souterrain

broch._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS] A style of the tower kind: a drystone round tower, double-walled, a souterrain (an underground passage) as its delve; lichen and moss (§DI).

cliff_dwelling.source: The alcove towns of the Ancestral Puebloans (Cliff Palace and Balcony House at Mesa Verde, Betatakin, Keet Seel) and the great kiva at Aztec Ruins; notes only (§BO)

kivas.form: round sunken rooms with a firebox and a vent

delve.rooms: the great kiva, then stores cut into the alcove's back
delve.way_out: a ladder to the alcove's rim

cliff_dwelling.smoke: out the kivas' vents and the roof hatches
cliff_dwelling._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS.4] Mike's second batch, 3 Oct 21:27: a town of stone rooms and round towers filling a sandstone alcove, and the great kiva. Its own kind at the mesa alcove nest (§CK): the alcove is its roof, so the stone stays nearly whole (§BQ).

brick_city.source: The mud-brick cities of the Mesopotamian floodplain (Babylon's Processional Way and gate, its tell of melted brick, the palace mound); notes only (§BO)

glazed.reliefs: animals in relief (aurochs, lions, a dragon of our own)

delve.rooms: the vaulted stores under the palace mound, a well
delve.way_out: the well shaft to the river bank

brick_city._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DS.6] Mike's second batch, 3 Oct 21:27: a city of mud brick on a desert river. What remains is the tell, a mound of melted brick with the foundation walls standing in it as a maze, the processional way between buttressed walls, the arched gate still standing with its blue glazed face (a saturated blue material that never glows, R8), the palace mound above the palms, the existing ziggurat at the centre.

hanging_gardens.source: Babylon's vaulted terraces (the brick vaults the diggers found) and the account of a king who planted mountain trees for a queen who missed her hills; notes only (§BO)

garden.ground: seedlings in every crack, moss and ferns where the water runs

delve.rooms: the vaulted galleries under the terraces, level by level, the channel running through them
delve.heart: the cistern where the water-lift stood
delve.way_out: the channel's mouth at the river

hanging_gardens.smoke: the gallery hearths vent through the terraces' drains
hanging_gardens._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DT] Mike, 3 Oct: its own kind, overgrown. A garden that outlived its gardeners: the channel still runs onto the top terrace (§BP), so the mountain trees the gardeners carried in grew huge and went wild (§CS/§CT's one exception placed by the generator), with the river's own palms and figs below. Water steps down the terraces (R6). Cedrus libani and Ficus carica are not in the catalogue yet (a fill for chat).

abbey.source: The roofless abbeys of northern England (Whitby, Rievaulx, Kirkstall, Fountains); notes only (§BO)

delve.rooms: the crypt and the undercroft under the east end
delve.way_out: the night stair up into the cloister

abbey.shafts: §DC's ruin kind through the lancets onto the grass
abbey._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DU] A great church with its roof gone: walls and arcades standing, lancets framing the sky, one tower, the floor turned to grass, the cloister in the turf, the warming house's chimney stack (smoke.json). Where §DC's shafts, §DI's residents and §DI's haunt meet. On a headland it is a landmark seen from the coast road (§DN).

colonnade.source: The columns of a burned great house near Port Gibson, Mississippi; notes only (§BO)
colonnade.avenue: a planted avenue of old oaks from the road (§DM.4), taller and older than the wild

delve.rooms: the brick cellar and the cistern under the house's footprint, half flooded

colonnade._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DV] The smallest monument in the set: the columns of a house of wood that burned, standing in a ring in a clearing among old oaks; §BQ to the letter, and the ending unnamed. §DI's wet row: vines on the columns, ferns at their feet, resurrection fern on the limbs (§CD).

temple_park.source: The brick-and-laterite temple precincts of the monsoon plains (Sukhothai, Ayutthaya); notes only (§BO)
temple_park.figures: seated, hands in the lap, faces worn smooth; nobody by name (§BO)

ponds.community: the sacred lotus's niche (§CS.6): warm still shallows
ponds.note: neither is in the catalogue yet: a fill for chat

delve.rooms: the great stupa's relic crypt reached by a shaft, the stores around it
delve.way_out: the shaft up the tower's side

temple_park.smoke: open fires only; the stupas vent nothing
temple_park._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DW] The open cousin of the temple city (§DR): flat, sunlit, in the monsoon dry forest, the sky over everything; roofless column rows (the roofs rotted, §BQ), stupas and towers, seated figures in niches, and lotus ponds with the towers reflected in them (R6). Never within 5 km of a temple city. §DI's dry row.

pillar_shrines.source: The sandstone pillar forests and tower karst of southern China, and the cut stairs and plank walks of the sacred mountains; notes only (§BO)
pillar_shrines.stairs: cut into the rock faces; the only way up (§AU: no wall climbing)

delve.rooms: a cave at the pillar's foot, then a stair cut up through it to the summit shrine
delve.way_out: a bridge, or the cliff stair

pillar_shrines.camp: canopy folk (§BT), who grow the root bridges back
pillar_shrines._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DY] A valley of pillars out of mist, a shrine on each top, bridges between them by span: stone arches stand, rope bridges are gone but for their posts (about one in six still hangs: first guess), living root bridges still grow (§BT). §BC's forks in three dimensions: you see the next shrine across a gap with no bridge, and the way is another pillar's stair or round through the mist. Bridges sway in the gust (§DA).

hewn_temple.source: The monolithic temple and cave halls at Ellora; notes only (§BO)

delve.rooms: the halls in the court walls, up the cut stairs between levels

hewn_temple._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DZ] A whole temple cut out of the hill from the top down, free in a court of living rock; found from above (the road comes along the rim and the ground opens at your feet, §BB's reveal inverted); the halls in the court walls are the delve as they stand (§CJ). Different from carved_cliffs (§DS.2), whose facades are cut into a face.

overgrowth._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DI] A ruin wears its place (Mike, 3 Oct by voice: "different mosses and plants and vines and stuff like overgrowing them"; "just dressing for now"). Dressing only: nothing to clear, no mechanic. What grows on it comes from the plants that really grow there (the community of the place, §CS; the biome gate §CA; the vines §CE; a nest's own plants §CM): moss on the stones, ferns in the cracks and at the foot, vines over the walls, grass and herbs along the wall tops, and lichen painted into the stone's own tile (look R9: detail in the albedo). by_moisture: how much of each by the place's moisture (the climate's 0-1), as rows of the columns; between rows they blend. shade_side_scale: the side away from the sun (north in the northern hemisphere, south in the southern) carries this much more moss and fern, as real walls do. age: older stone carries more (a monument against a camp's remains, §CK). cold_mean_c: where the year's mean is below this, only lichen and moss. Never a species the place can't grow: a desert ruin is nearly bare, a cloud-forest ruin green to the cornice. With §BQ's signatures and §CU's no-two-alike hearths, this is why two ruins of one kind are two places.

haunt._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DI] Haunted where the dead lie (Mike, 3 Oct by voice: "graveyards, mausoleums, it can be haunted. And so you might get glimpses of different ghosts which vanish"; "if you follow it around the corner ... it might just have vanished"). kinds: the ruins that can be (Ruins.Kind names; and the tomb and mausoleum rooms of any delve, §CJ); share: of those, how many are. A ghost is the shared cloaked rig (§0) in color at alpha, pale and a little see-through, with no light of its own (R8) and no sound; it never harms, never speaks and fills no meter. It is not a lurker (§CU): §BA's stage-3 shape at the edge of the light comes with the dread and its warnings, a ghost with none. when: only where the light is low (dusk, night, or a dark hall by day: sky visibility under low_light_visibility). where: at a corner, a doorway or the edge of your light, distance_m off, with an occluder within occluder_within_m of it to step behind. It is seen for seen_s, steps out of sight round that occluder, and is gone the moment it is out of view, so the corner you hurry round is empty. Never twice in a row at one spot. rarity: at most per_visit_max a visit, and about per_real_hour in a real hour spent in haunted places. It tells nothing (§BQ: the ending stays unnamed). (§DU adds the abbey: it has its graveyard and its tombs.)

root_trees._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DR] Trees that stand ON a ruin: a trunk on a gallery roof, a gopura or a wall top, its roots poured down over the lintel and the wall to the ground, bark pale against dark stone. The mechanism of §CL (the fig's roots gripping old stone) and §DJ (the oak door). species: the place's own (§CA, §CS) from genera; the big pale silk-cotton with the cascading roots (Tetrameles nudiflora) is a later one-line data fill for the jungle. by_kind: how many a monument carries: the temple city many (its signature), any other old monument in the listed biomes one or two (first guess, Mike's default). Only in the wet tropics (biomes). age: a camp's remains carry none.
